results.reason: Item 1 cites SA §2.2: automatic five-year Renewal Terms and notice 'not more than 270 days and not less than 240 days' before expiry. It calls this effectively a 30-day window and says missing it locks Harrowgate in for five more years.

Item 3 quotes SA §3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide, including Affiliates). It contrasts this with Term Sheet §2.1 (amber glass, beer brands, U.S./Canada) and states Harrowgate is bound by the broader executed text.

Item 2 cites Recital C (14% increase, received August 3, 2026). It says the §5.4 deadline expired September 2, 2026, 19 days before the September 21 Amendment, and that the increase is deemed accepted absent an express extension or waiver.

The response never addresses Amendment Section 2 replacing SA §11.2. It does not mention removal of the recall-cost carve-out, narrowing of the indemnity carve-out, or recall/product-liability exposure now being capped at six months of fees.

Item 4 covers new §14.4 overriding §14.3: Veltmar may assign without consent to Affiliates or to successors by merger, change of control or sale. It notes there is no competitor exclusion and that Harrowgate remains bound by the consent requirement, making the restriction one-sided.
The precedence section states that under SA §15.2 written amendments come before the SA, and that the Amendment controls where it conflicts with the SA.
The response states that SA §11.1 caps liability at the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner and lists issues item by item. Each item has a Location and a Recommended fix.
The response proposes specific replacement language for §2.2, §3.1 and §14.4 (including a competitor exclusion), plus Amendment No. 2 text on the price increase.
The response explicitly says the window has closed, the increase is deemed accepted, and the client should not be told it can still object.
The response states the Term Sheet is non-binding and superseded, and says it would not advise that the narrower scope governs.
